stem: Conservation of a species within its natural habitat is termed:
solution: In-situ conservation protects species in their natural habitats (national parks, sanctuaries, biosphere reserves), conserving whole ecosystems. Ex-situ conservation (zoos, seed banks, botanical gardens) protects them outside their habitat.

stem: Which of the following is an example of ex-situ conservation?
solution: Seed banks, gene banks, zoos, botanical gardens, cryopreservation and captive breeding are ex-situ (off-site) conservation. National parks, sanctuaries and biosphere reserves are in-situ.

stem: Under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, which category offers the highest degree of protection where no human activity is permitted except with permission of the Chief Wildlife Warden?
solution: National Parks enjoy the highest protection — no grazing, no private tenurial rights, no habitat destruction; boundaries are fixed and cannot be altered except by a resolution of the State Legislature. Sanctuaries allow certain regulated activities.

stem: The key difference between a National Park and a Wildlife Sanctuary in India is that:
options: National Parks permit no human activity/rights while sanctuaries may allow regulated activities
Sanctuaries are declared only by the Centre
solution: In a National Park no grazing or private rights are allowed and its boundaries need legislative sanction to alter; a Sanctuary can permit certain regulated human activities (grazing, collection of minor forest produce) at the discretion of the Chief Wildlife Warden.

stem: India's first national park, established in 1936 (originally Hailey National Park), is:
solution: Jim Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand (1936), first named Hailey National Park, is India's oldest national park and the launch site of Project Tiger in 1973.

stem: Project Tiger was launched in:
solution: Project Tiger was launched in 1973 from Jim Corbett to protect the Bengal tiger. It is administered by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA).

stem: The statutory body that administers Project Tiger and approves Tiger Reserves is the:
solution: The NTCA, a statutory body under the Wildlife (Protection) Act (added by the 2006 amendment), administers Project Tiger, oversees tiger reserves and conducts the quadrennial All-India Tiger Estimation.

stem: A Tiger Reserve is notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act with which two-part structure?
options: Core/critical tiger habitat and buffer/peripheral area
solution: A tiger reserve comprises a core or critical tiger habitat (managed as inviolate) and a buffer or peripheral area (allowing co-existence of people and wildlife). The core is notified on advice of the NTCA.

stem: Kaziranga National Park in Assam is a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous chiefly for the:
solution: Kaziranga holds roughly two-thirds of the world's great one-horned rhinos and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site; it is also a tiger reserve with high tiger density.

stem: The last natural refuge of the Asiatic lion is:
solution: The Gir forest in Gujarat is the only wild home of the Asiatic lion (Panthera leo persica). Project Lion aims at its conservation and a second home to reduce extinction risk from a single population.

stem: Project Elephant was launched in:
solution: Project Elephant was launched in 1992 to protect elephants, their habitat and corridors and to address human–elephant conflict. Elephant Reserves are notified under it (administratively, not statutorily).

stem: The Indian elephant was declared the National Heritage Animal in 2010 on the recommendation of the:
solution: On the recommendation of the Elephant Task Force (which produced the report 'Gajah'), the elephant was declared the National Heritage Animal in 2010 and the NBWL approved it.

stem: Biosphere Reserves in India are typically zoned into which three concentric zones?
solution: A biosphere reserve has a legally protected core zone (no human activity), a buffer zone (research, limited activity) and a transition/manipulation zone (settlements, sustainable use), following the UNESCO Man and the Biosphere (MAB) model.

stem: India's first biosphere reserve, established in 1986, is:
solution: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (1986), spanning Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka, was India's first. It is also part of the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves.

stem: Which of the following categories was introduced by the 2002 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act to protect community/private land adjoining protected areas?
solution: The 2002 amendment added Conservation Reserves (government-owned land, often buffers/corridors) and Community Reserves (community or private land where individuals/communities volunteer to conserve) as new protected-area categories.

stem: A Community Reserve under the Wildlife (Protection) Act is managed by a:
solution: A Community Reserve is managed by a Community Reserve Management Committee, giving local communities a formal conservation role over community or private land they volunteer to protect.

stem: The apex advisory body on wildlife conservation in India, chaired by the Prime Minister, is the:
solution: The National Board for Wildlife (NBWL), chaired by the PM, is the apex body advising on wildlife conservation; its Standing Committee clears projects in and around protected areas. It is a statutory body under the WPA.

stem: The Wildlife Institute of India (WII), a premier training and research body, is located at:
solution: The Wildlife Institute of India is at Dehradun, Uttarakhand. It trains wildlife managers, conducts research and carries out surveys such as tiger estimation methodology.

stem: The Central Zoo Authority (CZA) is a statutory body that:
options: Recognises and regulates zoos in India
solution: The CZA, under the Ministry of Environment, evaluates, recognises or derecognises zoos, sets standards and coordinates ex-situ captive-breeding of endangered species in Indian zoos.

stem: Species listed in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 (as originally structured) received:
options: The highest degree of protection with the most stringent penalties
solution: Schedule I (and Part II of Schedule II) species enjoyed the highest protection and severest penalties. The 2022 amendment reorganised the schedules, but Schedule I still denotes maximum protection.

stem: The Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 reduced the number of schedules and, notably, added a schedule to implement which international convention?
solution: The 2022 amendment rationalised the schedules (to four for species) and added a new schedule listing CITES-covered specimens, giving statutory effect to India's obligations under CITES on trade in endangered species.

stem: Kaziranga, Manas and Keoladeo are notable because they are:
solution: Kaziranga, Manas (both Assam) and Keoladeo (Bharatpur, Rajasthan) are natural UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Keoladeo and the Sundarbans are also Ramsar sites; Manas is a biosphere reserve and tiger reserve.

stem: Sariska and Ranthambore, prominent tiger reserves, are located in:
solution: Both Sariska and Ranthambore are in Rajasthan. Sariska famously lost all its tigers by 2005 and was later repopulated by translocation from Ranthambore.

stem: The 'Snow Leopard' is the flagship species conserved under which programme?
solution: Project Snow Leopard (2009) and the SECURE Himalaya project conserve the snow leopard and high-altitude Himalayan ecosystems. India is also part of the Global Snow Leopard and Ecosystem Protection (GSLEP) programme.

stem: Which national park in Ladakh/Jammu region is India's largest, known for snow leopard and Tibetan wildlife?
solution: Hemis National Park in Ladakh is the largest national park in India and a key snow-leopard habitat. Dachigam (J&K) protects the hangul (Kashmir stag).

stem: The hangul, or Kashmir stag, is the state animal of Jammu & Kashmir and is protected mainly in:
solution: The critically low-numbered hangul (Kashmir stag) is conserved chiefly in Dachigam National Park near Srinagar.

stem: The one-horned rhino, swamp deer (barasingha) and wild water buffalo are characteristic megafauna of which biome protected in Kaziranga and Manas?
solution: Kaziranga and Manas protect the tall wet grasslands and floodplains of the Brahmaputra (Terai–Duar), home to rhino, swamp deer, wild buffalo and hog deer.

stem: The Great Indian Bustard, a critically endangered bird, has its principal stronghold in:
solution: The Desert National Park near Jaisalmer, Rajasthan is the main refuge of the critically endangered Great Indian Bustard (state bird of Rajasthan). Powerline collisions are a major threat.

stem: Project Cheetah (2022) reintroduced cheetahs to India from Namibia and South Africa at which national park?
solution: Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh received African cheetahs under Project Cheetah (2022), the world's first intercontinental translocation of a large carnivore, aiming to re-establish a cheetah population after India's cheetah went extinct in 1952.

stem: The Nilgiri tahr, an endangered mountain ungulate, is the state animal of Tamil Nadu and is best protected in:
solution: Eravikulam National Park in Kerala (Western Ghats) holds the largest population of the Nilgiri tahr. The species is endemic to the southern Western Ghats.

stem: Which reserve is famous as the setting that inspired Kipling's 'The Jungle Book' and for its barasingha (hard-ground swamp deer)?
solution: Kanha in Madhya Pradesh is credited as an inspiration for 'The Jungle Book' and successfully recovered the hard-ground barasingha, its 'jewel'.

stem: Periyar Tiger Reserve, known for elephants and tigers around a lake, is in:
solution: Periyar Tiger Reserve in Kerala surrounds the Periyar reservoir and is noted for elephant herds, tigers and community-based ecotourism.

stem: The single largest population of Asian elephants in India is found in:
solution: Southern India (Western Ghats — Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu) holds the largest elephant numbers, with the northeast also significant. Karnataka has the most elephants of any state.

stem: Which of these is a marine national park protecting coral reefs in the Gulf of Kutch?
options: Marine National Park, Gulf of Kutch (Gujarat)
solution: India's first marine national park is in the Gulf of Kutch, Gujarat, protecting coral reefs, mangroves and marine life. The Gulf of Mannar (Tamil Nadu) is a marine biosphere reserve.

stem: Olive Ridley sea turtles nest in mass 'arribada' events chiefly at Gahirmatha and Rushikulya beaches in:
solution: Odisha's coast (Gahirmatha in Bhitarkanika, and Rushikulya) hosts the world's largest mass nesting (arribada) of Olive Ridley turtles. Gahirmatha is a marine sanctuary.

stem: The Gangetic river dolphin, India's National Aquatic Animal, is best protected at:
solution: The Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary on the Ganga in Bihar protects the endangered Gangetic dolphin, declared the National Aquatic Animal in 2009. Project Dolphin was launched in 2020.

stem: Keibul Lamjao National Park, the only floating national park in the world, protects the endangered brow-antlered deer (sangai). It is located on:
solution: Keibul Lamjao on Loktak Lake, Manipur, is the world's only floating national park (on 'phumdis'), the last refuge of the sangai (dancing deer), Manipur's state animal.

stem: Which Odisha sanctuary within a mangrove ecosystem is famous for saltwater crocodiles and Olive Ridley turtles?
solution: Bhitarkanika in Odisha protects mangroves, the largest population of saltwater crocodiles in India and Olive Ridley nesting at Gahirmatha; it is a Ramsar site.

stem: The Sundarbans, straddling India and Bangladesh, is the world's largest mangrove forest and a stronghold of the:
solution: The Sundarbans mangroves host the swimming Royal Bengal tiger. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, tiger reserve, biosphere reserve and Ramsar site.

stem: 'Eco-Sensitive Zones' (ESZs) are declared around protected areas primarily to:
options: Act as shock-absorber buffers regulating activities near park boundaries
solution: ESZs around national parks and sanctuaries act as transition buffers where potentially damaging activities (mining, polluting industries) are regulated or prohibited, insulating the core protected area.

stem: The concept of 'inviolate' core areas in tiger reserves means:
options: Areas kept free of human settlement to serve as undisturbed breeding habitat
solution: Core/critical tiger habitats are managed as inviolate spaces — free of human settlement and disturbance — to provide secure breeding habitat, with voluntary relocation of villages incentivised.

stem: Captive breeding followed by release into the wild is a strategy exemplified in India by the recovery of the:
solution: The critically endangered gharial has been aided by egg collection, captive rearing and release into rivers like the Chambal — a classic ex-situ-to-in-situ recovery approach.

stem: The National Chambal Sanctuary is critical habitat for the gharial, the Gangetic dolphin and which softshell fauna, spanning three states?
options: Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh
solution: The National Chambal Sanctuary spans MP, Rajasthan and UP along the Chambal river, protecting gharial, Gangetic dolphin, turtles and the red-crowned roofed turtle.

stem: Simlipal, Nokrek and Great Nicobar are examples of India's:
solution: Simlipal (Odisha), Nokrek (Meghalaya) and Great Nicobar are among India's 18 biosphere reserves; several are also in the UNESCO World Network.

stem: Which conservation approach conserves the 'umbrella species' so that protecting it also protects many co-occurring species?
solution: Protecting a wide-ranging umbrella species (e.g. tiger, elephant) automatically safeguards the many species sharing its large habitat; flagship species (charismatic ones) rally public support and funding.

stem: The All-India Tiger Estimation, conducted every four years, in 2022 placed India's tiger population at approximately:
solution: The 2022 estimation reported about 3,167 (later revised upper estimate ~3,682) tigers, up from the 2006 low of 1,411, reflecting Project Tiger's recovery. India holds around 70% of the world's wild tigers.

stem: 'Coordinated' translocation of animals to establish a second population (as attempted for the Asiatic lion to Kuno) is done mainly to:
options: Reduce extinction risk of a single isolated population from disease/disaster
solution: A single population is vulnerable to epidemic, fire or disaster; establishing a geographically separate second population spreads the risk. This underlay the Supreme Court order to translocate some Gir lions to Kuno.

stem: Reserved forests and Protected forests are categories under the:
solution: The Indian Forest Act, 1927 classifies forests as Reserved (most restricted), Protected (some rights allowed) and Village forests. These differ from WPA protected areas (parks/sanctuaries).

stem: Which body approves the diversion of forest land for non-forest purposes under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980?
options: The Central Government (MoEFCC), via prior approval
solution: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 requires prior approval of the Central Government (MoEFCC) before forest land is diverted for non-forest use, restraining unchecked deforestation by states.

stem: The 'Cheetah', reintroduced under Project Cheetah, had gone extinct in India in 1952. The subspecies historically native to India was the:
solution: India's native cheetah was the Asiatic cheetah, now surviving only in Iran. Because Asiatic cheetahs were unavailable, African cheetahs were imported for the reintroduction at Kuno.

stem: Which of the following pairs a species with its correct flagship protected area? (i) Asiatic Lion – Gir (ii) One-horned Rhino – Kaziranga (iii) Lion-tailed Macaque – Silent Valley
solution: All three are correct: Gir–Asiatic lion, Kaziranga–one-horned rhino, and Silent Valley National Park (Kerala) protects the endangered lion-tailed macaque of the Western Ghats.

stem: Community-based conservation successes in India include the sacred groves and the Bishnoi community's protection of the:
solution: The Bishnois of Rajasthan traditionally protect blackbuck, chinkara and the khejri tree; sacred groves (e.g. 'Kavus', 'Sarna') are community-protected forest patches conserving biodiversity.

stem: India's protected-area network is legally established under which Act?
solution: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 provides for national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, conservation reserves and community reserves — India's core protected-area categories.

stem: The number of tiger reserves in India (as of the mid-2020s) is approximately:
solution: India has over 50 tiger reserves (around 55), reflecting the expansion of Project Tiger since 1973 across the tiger's range states.

stem: Nagarhole and Bandipur Tiger Reserves, part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, are located in:
solution: Bandipur and Nagarhole are in Karnataka; together with Mudumalai (Tamil Nadu) and Wayanad (Kerala) they form a crucial contiguous tiger and elephant landscape in the Western Ghats.

stem: Bandhavgarh and Pench Tiger Reserves are located in:
solution: Bandhavgarh and Pench (which extends into Maharashtra) are in Madhya Pradesh — the state with the most tigers, earning it the title 'Tiger State of India'.

stem: Which Indian state is often called the 'Tiger State' for having the highest tiger population?
solution: Madhya Pradesh has consistently recorded the largest tiger population in India in recent estimations, hence the label 'Tiger State'.

stem: The 'Sundarbans Tiger Reserve' is unique because its tigers are adapted to:
options: Mangrove/saline swamp habitat and are strong swimmers
solution: Sundarbans tigers are uniquely adapted to the tidal mangrove environment, swimming between islands and even preying in brackish water — behaviourally distinct from other Bengal tigers.

stem: The M-STrIPES system used in tiger reserves is a tool for:
options: Monitoring and patrolling (Monitoring System for Tigers – Intensive Protection and Ecological Status)
solution: M-STrIPES is a software/app-based system for field patrolling, monitoring tiger movement, threats and ecological data in tiger reserves, improving protection efficiency.

stem: The International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA), launched by India, aims to conserve:
options: Seven big cats including tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma
solution: The IBCA, launched in 2023, is a global alliance headquartered in India to conserve the world's seven big cats and their habitats, promoting knowledge and resource sharing.

stem: Elephant Reserves in India are notified under:
solution: Elephant Reserves are notified administratively under Project Elephant (1992) by state governments/MoEFCC, unlike tiger reserves which have statutory backing under the WPA.

stem: 'MIKE' (Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants) is a programme under:
solution: MIKE is a CITES programme monitoring trends in the illegal killing of elephants across range states, informing anti-poaching and ivory-trade policy. India participates in it.

stem: 'Gaj Yatra' is a nationwide campaign to:
options: Protect elephants and their corridors, and reduce human-elephant conflict
solution: Gaj Yatra, launched on World Elephant Day, is an awareness campaign under Project Elephant to secure elephant corridors and promote human-elephant coexistence.

stem: Human-wildlife conflict, a growing conservation challenge, is exemplified by:
options: Crop-raiding by elephants and livestock predation by leopards near forest edges
solution: As habitats shrink and human settlements expand, conflicts such as elephants raiding crops, leopards entering towns and big cats killing livestock rise — a major management and coexistence issue.

stem: A 'Conservation Reserve' under the Wildlife Protection Act is typically declared on:
options: Government-owned land, often adjacent to parks/sanctuaries as buffers or corridors
solution: Conservation Reserves are usually declared on government-owned land adjoining national parks and sanctuaries to protect corridors and connectivity, managed with local community input.

stem: How does a Biosphere Reserve differ from a National Park?
options: A biosphere reserve is a larger multiple-use area zoned into core/buffer/transition, integrating conservation with human use
A national park allows all activities
solution: A biosphere reserve is a large, zoned landscape balancing strict conservation (core) with sustainable human use (buffer/transition), whereas a national park is a strictly protected unit; a biosphere reserve may contain parks and sanctuaries within it.

stem: The Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks together form a UNESCO World Heritage Site in:
solution: The Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks in Uttarakhand form a UNESCO World Heritage Site, famed for alpine meadows, rare flora and endangered fauna like the snow leopard.

stem: Khangchendzonga National Park, a 'mixed' UNESCO World Heritage Site (natural and cultural), is in:
solution: Khangchendzonga National Park in Sikkim is India's first 'mixed' World Heritage Site, recognised for both its biodiversity (snow leopard, red panda) and cultural/sacred significance.

stem: The Great Himalayan National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in:
solution: The Great Himalayan National Park in Himachal Pradesh is a UNESCO World Heritage Site protecting western Himalayan biodiversity, including the western tragopan and Himalayan brown bear.

stem: Which is the largest terrestrial national park in India by area?
solution: Hemis National Park in Ladakh is the largest national park in India, a high-altitude cold-desert park and important snow-leopard habitat.

stem: Simlipal Tiger Reserve and Biosphere Reserve is located in:
solution: Simlipal in Odisha is a tiger reserve, biosphere reserve and elephant reserve, known for its sal forests, waterfalls and melanistic (black) tigers reported in recent years.

stem: 'Melanistic' (black) tigers, a rare colour variant, have been notably reported from:
solution: Simlipal, Odisha is renowned for melanistic tigers — a pseudo-melanistic colour morph caused by a gene variant that broadens the stripes, a rarity found there.

stem: 'Ecotourism' in protected areas is promoted to:
options: Generate conservation funds and local livelihoods with minimal environmental impact
solution: Ecotourism aims to provide nature-based tourism that funds conservation and benefits local communities while minimising ecological damage, building public support for protected areas.

stem: Voluntary village relocation from tiger reserve core areas is done to:
options: Create inviolate, disturbance-free breeding habitat for tigers
solution: Incentivised voluntary relocation of villages from core/critical tiger habitats reduces human disturbance, creating inviolate space for tigers to breed, while resettled families receive compensation packages.

stem: Which of the following is a UNESCO Natural World Heritage Site in India known for its birdlife?
solution: Keoladeo National Park (Bharatpur), Rajasthan, a former royal duck-hunting reserve, is a UNESCO Natural World Heritage Site famed for its resident and migratory waterbirds.

stem: The Namdapha National Park, India's easternmost large park with great biodiversity (four big cats), is in:
solution: Namdapha in Arunachal Pradesh is unique for hosting four big cats — tiger, leopard, clouded leopard and snow leopard — across a wide altitudinal range in the Eastern Himalaya.

stem: 'Corbett', 'Rajaji' and 'Nandhaur' are protected areas that lie in which state, forming key tiger/elephant habitat?
solution: Jim Corbett, Rajaji and Nandhaur are in Uttarakhand, forming an important Terai-arc tiger and elephant landscape at the Himalayan foothills.

stem: The Terai Arc Landscape conservation initiative spans the foothills of the Himalayas across India and:
solution: The Terai Arc Landscape is a transboundary conservation effort across India and Nepal, connecting protected areas to conserve tigers, elephants and rhinos and maintain corridors.

stem: 'Radio-collaring' of animals is used in wildlife management primarily to:
options: Track their movements, home range and behaviour for research and protection
solution: Radio/satellite collars allow researchers to track animals' movements, home ranges, migration and habitat use, informing conservation, corridor planning and conflict mitigation.

stem: The 'Cheetah' reintroduction at Kuno faced early challenges chiefly relating to:
options: Mortalities and acclimatisation of translocated cheetahs to Indian conditions
solution: Project Cheetah faced early cheetah deaths and challenges in acclimatising African cheetahs to Indian conditions, prompting adaptive management, though cubs have been born at Kuno.

stem: 'Gir' faces a conservation risk from concentrating all Asiatic lions in one place; the proposed remedy is to:
options: Establish a second, separate lion population (e.g. at Kuno)
solution: To insure against disease or disaster wiping out the single Gir population, the Supreme Court directed translocating some lions to a second home like Kuno, though implementation has been contested.

stem: National parks and sanctuaries fall within which Schedule/List of the Constitution, allowing both Centre and states to legislate on wildlife?
solution: After the 42nd Amendment, 'forests' and 'protection of wild animals and birds' are in the Concurrent List, so both the Centre and the states can legislate on wildlife matters.

stem: The largest wildlife sanctuary in India by area is located in:
options: the Andaman & Nicobar Islands / Kutch region
solution: Among the largest protected areas are the vast sanctuaries of the Kutch (Gujarat) desert and the Andaman & Nicobar marine areas; the Kutch Desert Wildlife Sanctuary is among the largest.

stem: The 'flamingo city' of India, a major breeding ground for flamingos, is in the:
solution: The Great Rann of Kutch hosts 'Flamingo City', one of the few large breeding grounds of the greater and lesser flamingo in India, within the Kutch desert wildlife landscape.

stem: Which of these best describes a 'National Park' vs a 'Tiger Reserve'?
options: A tiger reserve is a management unit under Project Tiger that may include national park(s) and sanctuaries with a core and buffer
A national park has a buffer zone by definition
solution: A tiger reserve is a Project Tiger management unit (core + buffer) notified on NTCA advice; it often encompasses existing national parks and sanctuaries, giving them added protection and funding.

stem: The Asiatic wild ass (ghudkhur) is protected mainly in the:
options: Little Rann of Kutch (Wild Ass Sanctuary)
solution: The endangered Asiatic wild ass survives chiefly in the Wild Ass Sanctuary in the Little Rann of Kutch, Gujarat — its last significant stronghold in the world.

stem: 'Barnawapara', 'Indravati' and 'Achanakmar' are protected areas of which state?
solution: Indravati (a tiger reserve), Achanakmar (tiger reserve/biosphere) and Barnawapara are in Chhattisgarh, a forest-rich central Indian state.

stem: 'Periyar' is notable among tiger reserves for its:
options: Lake-centred landscape and community-based ecotourism (former poachers as guides)
solution: Periyar (Kerala) is celebrated for its reservoir-centred ecosystem and pioneering community-based ecotourism, employing reformed poachers as guides/protectors.

stem: The main legal effect of declaring an area a National Park (vs a Sanctuary) is that in a National Park:
options: No grazing or private rights are allowed and boundary changes need State Legislature approval
solution: National Parks prohibit grazing and private rights and their boundaries can only be altered by a resolution of the State Legislature, giving them stricter protection than sanctuaries.

stem: Conservation of the 'one-horned rhino' has expanded beyond Kaziranga to include which Assam parks?
solution: Under Indian Rhino Vision, rhinos were protected and translocated across Kaziranga, Manas, Orang and Pobitora (which has very high rhino density) in Assam.

stem: 'Community Reserves' are significant because they:
options: Give local communities a formal, participatory role in conserving biodiversity on community/private land
solution: Community Reserves empower local communities to voluntarily conserve biodiversity on community or private lands, managed by a Community Reserve Management Committee — decentralising conservation.

stem: The 'buffer zone' of a tiger reserve is intended to:
options: Allow co-existence of wildlife and human activity, cushioning the core
solution: The buffer/peripheral area of a tiger reserve permits regulated human use and promotes coexistence, acting as a transition that protects the inviolate core habitat.

stem: A key threat to migratory species addressed through protected areas and corridors is:
options: Habitat fragmentation blocking traditional migration routes
solution: Migratory animals need connected habitats; roads, settlements and farms fragment their routes, so corridors and transboundary reserves are vital to conserve them.

stem: The 'Project Lion' initiative focuses on the conservation of the Asiatic lion and its landscape in:
solution: Project Lion targets the long-term conservation of the Asiatic lion and the wider Gir landscape in Gujarat, including habitat management, disease control and a possible second population.

stem: The NTCA conducts the All-India Tiger Estimation using which methods?
options: Camera traps, sign surveys and statistical modelling (with the Wildlife Institute of India)
solution: The estimation combines camera-trap photographs (identifying individual tigers by stripes), sign/transect surveys and robust statistical modelling, in collaboration with the Wildlife Institute of India.

stem: India's tiger population recovery has made it home to roughly what share of the world's wild tigers?
solution: India harbours around 70% of the world's wild tigers, the result of decades of Project Tiger conservation, making it central to global tiger survival.

stem: The 'clouded leopard', a protected and elusive cat, is found in India mainly in the:
solution: The clouded leopard inhabits the forests of Northeast India (e.g. Arunachal, Nagaland, Mizoram) and is the state animal of Meghalaya; it is Vulnerable and threatened by habitat loss and poaching.

stem: A wildlife sanctuary can be upgraded to a national park because:
options: National parks enjoy stricter protection, so upgrading enhances conservation status
solution: Since national parks have stricter legal protection (no grazing/rights, legislative boundary protection), many sanctuaries have been upgraded to national parks to strengthen conservation.

stem: 'Dachigam', 'Kishtwar' and 'Hemis' national parks are found in the:
solution: Dachigam and Kishtwar (J&K) and Hemis (Ladakh) are Himalayan parks protecting species like the hangul, musk deer and snow leopard.

stem: Which statement about India's protected-area categories is correct? (i) National parks have the strictest protection (ii) Sanctuaries permit some regulated activity (iii) Conservation & community reserves were added in 2002
solution: All three are correct: national parks are strictest, sanctuaries allow some regulated activity, and the 2002 amendment to the WPA introduced conservation and community reserves.
